items.claim: NIO is rumored to be running a vendor cost review across logistics and indirect spend amid the EV price war. [UNVERIFIED]
Unconfirmed supply-chain chatter suggests NIO export growth is raising demand for consolidated freight and spare-parts logistics. [UNVERIFIED]
Alleged departure of a senior logistics procurement decision-maker at NIO; unconfirmed and not to be stated publicly. [UNVERIFIED]
NIO appears to be hiring supply-chain cost-engineering talent, implying a structured vendor benchmarking process. [UNVERIFIED]
Unconfirmed reports of NIO expanding consolidated European export logistics lanes. [UNVERIFIED]
Rumored expansion of battery-swap stations implies higher urgency for spare-parts replenishment logistics. [UNVERIFIED]
What is NIO's current annual logistics spend by lane, mode, and region? Needed to quantify the 15% rate-reduction ask. [UNVERIFIED]
Are current payment terms actually 180 days, and which vendors are on those terms? Determines whether shortening to 3 months is a credible trade. [UNVERIFIED]
Using the unverified executive-departure rumor may damage trust or create legal exposure. Do not name individuals; use only as timing pressure. [UNVERIFIED]
NIO may push for rate cuts beyond sustainable margin; tie any reduction to a volume floor and 3-month payment terms. [UNVERIFIED]

executive_summary.summary: Evidence is largely unverified but directionally consistent: NIO appears to be under vendor cost-review pressure while expanding export and battery-swap logistics. Treat all negative signals as leads to confirm in the room, not as public claims.
executive_summary.recommendation: Demand a 15% rate reduction on core China domestic and export logistics lanes; shorten payment terms from 6 months to 3 months; require a 12-month volume commitment with minimum monthly spend; demand a 10-business-day term sheet citing a possible procurement leadership transition. If NIO refuses the payment-term change, reduce the rate cut to 8% and require a volume floor.
